sections.html:
Jasper, on the Patoka River, is the seat and biggest city of Dubois County in southwest Indiana. The 2020 census counted 43,637 people in the county, up from 41,889 in 2010, with 17,412 households and 16,703 residents in Jasper. The median age is 41.2.

Jasper bills itself as the Wood Capital of the World. Manufacturing is the largest employer by sector, followed by retail and health care, and furniture and cabinet makers such as Jasper Group, Kimball International and MasterBrand Cabinets anchor the local job market. Steady employment keeps demand for houses fairly even, but older and outdated homes still sell slowly. Patoka Lake, along the eastern edge, and part of Hoosier National Forest add rural and lakeside parcels to the mix, and those often carry different assessments than in-town lots.

The numbers point to slow, steady growth. The county added about 1,750 residents over the decade and the 2025 estimate is 44,016, while Jasper rose from 12,100 in 2000 to 15,038 in 2010 and 16,703 in 2020. Huntingburg and Ferdinand are the other named towns, and Vincennes University has a Jasper campus, which supports a modest base of renters and first-time buyers. For a seller, that means a clean, correctly assessed house in town should draw local interest, while a rural parcel or an older home may take longer.

sections.h2: The Assessor's office and yearly dates
sections.html:
The Assessor works from One Courthouse Square, Jasper, IN 47546. Reach the office at 812-481-7010 or assessor@duboiscountyin.org. Doors are open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Four dates repeat every year:

  • January 1 is the assessment date.
  • April 1 is the deadline for Form 136 exemption applications.
  • May 15 is when business personal property returns are due, or the next business day if it falls on a weekend.
  • December 31 is the deadline for affidavits about destroyed or removed property.

Projects that need no building permit still require a Notice of Assessment Registration, and failing to file brings a $100 civil penalty. If you added or tore down a structure, tell the assessor before a buyer's review so the record matches what is on the lot.

Exemption applications deserve a reminder too. If a house or lot qualifies for an exemption on Form 136, the April 1 deadline is firm, so a seller who plans to list in the spring should check the filing before that date. Business owners who also own the building should note the May 15 return, since the same office handles both.

The assessor's website links Form 130 under the heading "Appeal an assessment." June 15 is the deadline, counted in the year the notice or the tax bill is mailed.

A single petition covers a single parcel. An informal meeting with the assessor comes first. If it does not settle things, the county board of appeals (the PTABOA) must hear the case within 180 days, after mailing notice at least 30 days ahead. Missing the hearing with no valid continuance can cost $50. A loss at that level can go to the Indiana Board of Tax Review on Form 131.

Gather proof before the meeting: an appraisal, sale prices for similar homes nearby, or repair estimates. If you are selling soon, remember that a lower assessment also helps a buyer see a lower yearly cost.

Dubois County usually holds its tax sale in September or October for parcels with a balance dating to the spring of the prior year or earlier. In mid-July the Auditor's office normally mails a certified letter to each listed owner.

Dubois County tax sale steps
StepWhat happens
Added costA $130.00 tax sale charge is added to each parcel's amount due
PublicationNames are published in local newspapers if taxes remain unpaid
SaleOnline or live at the County Courthouse
Minimum bidTotal owed on the parcel through the current year
PaymentHigh bidder pays the Treasurer the same day, in cash or certified funds
RedemptionThe owner has one year, then the Auditor issues a deed to the certificate holder

Owners can pay right up to the time of the sale. The Treasurer is at One Courthouse Square, Jasper, at 812-481-7080 or treasurer@duboiscountyin.org, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

The state sets two installments, May 10 and November 10, and a weekend date moves to the next business day.

Pay within 30 days of the due date with no earlier delinquency and the penalty is 5%. Otherwise it is 10%, and later installments can add more 10% penalties.

The standard homestead deduction has been 60% of assessed value up to $48,000, filed by January 5, and the rule changed effective January 1, 2025. Confirm today's figure with the Assessor before you quote it to a buyer.

Why it matters at sale time: a buyer's monthly cost depends on whether the deduction is in place, and a home that stops being a primary residence can lose it. Put the question to the Assessor before the listing goes live and print the answer for your file.

Inherited houses, dated interiors and unpaid tax are the usual stories in Dubois County. The state's sales disclosure form must go through the assessor before the deed reaches the auditor, and every parcel gets its own.

  • Ask the Treasurer for the balance and any tax sale charge.
  • Look at the assessor's records for added or removed structures.
  • Collect estate documents and earlier tax bills.
  • Choose between repairing and selling as is.

A cash purchase can close fast, with the title company paying taxes from your proceeds.

Timing can save real money. A parcel with a balance from the spring of the prior year or earlier can land on the sale list, and the $130.00 charge attaches once it is listed. If you are near that point, pay or sell before the July letter goes out. Owners can still pay up to the moment of the sale, but the added charge does not go away.

Bring a short folder to your closing agent: the newest tax bill, any estate documents, and a note of every building you added or tore down. When the assessor's card matches what a buyer sees on the lot, the sales disclosure form moves faster, and a missing registration or an old structure still on the card can be cleared up before it holds up the deed.

For an inherited house, start with the paperwork. Confirm the names on the deed, ask the Treasurer what is owed on each parcel, and decide whether the heirs will sell as is. If the house has stood empty, expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at the roof, the heating and the plumbing, and be ready to price accordingly or accept an offer that takes the house in its current state.

faqs.q: Where is the Dubois County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: At One Courthouse Square, Jasper, IN 47546, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The phone is 812-481-7010.

faqs.q: When does the Dubois County tax sale happen?
faqs.a: Usually in September or October. A certified letter normally reaches listed owners in mid-July, and owners can pay up to the time of the sale.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem Dubois County property after a tax sale?
faqs.a: One year. After that the Auditor's office issues a deed to the certificate holder.

faqs.q: What is the Dubois County tax sale charge?
faqs.a: A $130.00 charge is added to each parcel's amount due once it is listed for the sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Dubois County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance and penalties come out of your proceeds at closing, and selling before the sale date avoids the added charge.
